sketches.mechanism: The `object` declaration creates a singleton — exactly one instance can ever exist, and it is initialized lazily the first time it is accessed.
sketches.resonance: Loneliness is not constructed; it simply exists the moment you look for it, and there can only ever be one.

sketches.mechanism: A weak reference does not keep the referenced object alive; when no strong references remain, it becomes nil automatically.
sketches.resonance: Holding someone weakly means they can vanish at any moment without your permission — the language enforces the impermanence of what you refuse to grip.

sketches.mechanism: The `never` return type indicates a function that can never successfully return — it must throw or loop forever.
sketches.resonance: The act of forgetting is promised but structurally impossible to complete; the type system guarantees it will never resolve.
